title: Why constructors are not overridden
answer: Constructors are not inherited, so they cannot be overridden. A subclass declares its own constructors, and those constructors may invoke superclass constructors to initialize inherited state. Overriding applies to inherited instance methods with compatible signatures, not constructors. AeroTopo's `Orthomosaic` constructor is a new constructor for the subclass; it calls `super(id, tiles)` but does not override either `Product` constructor.
